title: App Surface Owner Decision Baseline Semantics
authorityNotice: This artefact records USF-native owner-decision semantics for app-surface planning. It records evaluated owner decisions for bounded local app-surface implementation. It does not authorise provider account setup, credential setup, deployment, store submission, legal compliance claims, privacy compliance claims, production readiness claims, or live-provider readiness claims.
globalNonClaims: Bounded local app-surface implementation is governed by docs/architecture/pre-ui-repository-readiness-realisation.json and the applicable implementation gates.
Dependency installation is governed by bounded local implementation scope and frozen dependency policy.
No provider account setup is authorised.
No privacy compliance readiness is claimed.
No live external provider readiness is claimed.

decisions.decision: Authoritative durable mobile client state must use a SQLite-class transactional store when offline persistence is required. Secrets, tokens, and credentials must use operating-system secure storage. AsyncStorage-class and MMKV-class stores may be used only for non-authoritative UI cache or preference data when later implementation authority explicitly permits that use.
permits: semantic planning for SQLite-class durable storage
semantic planning for operating-system secure storage
forbids: treating AsyncStorage-class or MMKV-class stores as authoritative records by default
storing secrets outside operating-system secure storage
installing any storage dependency from this decision alone
downstreamEvaluationAndExecutionRequirem: retention and purge proof expectations exist
privacy and security validators cover the chosen store

decisions.decision: Expo managed configuration with CNG or prebuild is the preferred mobile adapter posture. Bare native project ownership is an exception path only when a USF semantic requirement, security requirement, native capability requirement, or proof requirement cannot be satisfied through the managed CNG path.
permits: semantic planning for Expo managed CNG
exception analysis for bare native requirements
forbids: generating native projects from this decision alone
treating bare native as the default posture
claiming App Store or Google Play readiness
downstreamEvaluationAndExecutionRequirem: native capability bridge semantics are mapped

decisions.decision: Next.js deployment remains provider-neutral at the semantic layer. Cloudflare, Netlify, Vercel, and self-hosted options remain candidates, but no provider is canonical until the CDN/provider gate verifies runtime support, evidence collection, secrets handling, rollback, logs, data residency, and owner approval.
permits: provider comparison against USF evidence requirements
route and deployment semantics that are independent of one provider
forbids: deploying to any provider from this decision alone
creating provider credentials
claiming CDN readiness
downstreamEvaluationAndExecutionRequirem: owner-approved provider credentials exist outside this semantic decision

decisions.decision: The CDN provider posture is provider-neutral until a later implementation gate selects a concrete provider. Any selected provider must satisfy custom domain, TLS, preview deployment, branch control, environment, secret, logging, rollback, purge, cache, provenance, and evidence requirements before deployment readiness can be claimed.
forbids: DNS changes from this decision alone
provider account setup from this decision alone
deployment readiness claims

decisions.decision: The initial localisation planning baseline is English with en-US and en-AU locale profiles. This is a semantic planning baseline only, not a public launch approval. Any public country, language, store listing, privacy text, terms text, or regional feature claim requires external review and the relevant release gates close.
permits: locale fallback and translation-key validation planning
forbids: public launch country approval from this decision alone
legal-text readiness claims
store listing readiness claims
downstreamEvaluationAndExecutionRequirem: privacy and terms text evidence exists

decisions.decision: Ads are disabled by default for the initial app-surface posture. No ads provider is selected for implementation. Any future ad provider must be approved through privacy, consent, child-directed policy, SDK registry, telemetry, and external review gates before integration.
forbids: ad SDK integration from this decision alone
ad provider account setup
personalised ads readiness claims

decisions.decision: Ad Manager and alternative ad-serving platforms are out of scope for the initial posture. They may be reconsidered only through a later owner decision with provider-specific data, consent, regional, SDK, validator, and proof analysis.
forbids: Ad Manager setup
alternative ad platform setup
ad-serving readiness claims
downstreamEvaluationAndExecutionRequirem: ads provider model is reopened or superseded

decisions.decision: Apple IAP and Google Play Billing are out of scope for the initial posture. Paid digital goods, subscriptions, entitlement fulfilment, and billing provider integrations require separate semantic authority, store policy review, validator coverage, and proof evidence.
forbids: billing implementation
store product setup
subscription readiness claims

decisions.decision: The initial store monetisation posture is free with no ads, no paid app price, no in-app products, and no subscriptions. Any monetisation model requires later owner approval, privacy and consent mapping where applicable, store policy review, validator coverage, and proof evidence.
forbids: paid app setup
in-app product setup
subscription setup
ads monetisation setup

decisions.decision: Apple and Google store accounts, signing authority, release approval, and credential custody remain owner-controlled. Agents must not create accounts, assign roles, create signing credentials, or submit builds. Any release requires explicit human owner approval and auditable evidence.
forbids: agent-created store accounts
agent-created signing credentials
automated store submission without explicit owner approval

decisions.decision: EAS Build and EAS Submit are the preferred managed mobile build and submission path after implementation authority exists. Self-hosted or Fastlane-based flows remain fallback options only where evidence, security, cost, or platform requirements justify them.
permits: fallback comparison for self-hosted and Fastlane flows
forbids: EAS setup from this decision alone
CI secret setup from this decision alone
build execution from this decision alone

decisions.decision: Certificate pinning is not enabled by default. Platform TLS, correct certificate validation, HTTPS-only transport, and web security headers remain the baseline. Pinning may be introduced only with a documented threat model, rotation procedure, recovery procedure, provider compatibility, validator coverage, and proof evidence.
forbids: pinning implementation from this decision alone
security certification claims
readiness claims without rotation and recovery proof
downstreamEvaluationAndExecutionRequirem: rotation and recovery procedures are validated

decisions.decision: No third-party analytics or crash provider is selected by default. App-surface diagnostics must be privacy-safe, consent-aware, data-minimising, and evidence-backed. A concrete provider requires later owner approval, SDK data inventory, consent mapping, retention mapping, validator coverage, and proof evidence.
forbids: analytics SDK installation from this decision alone
crash SDK installation from this decision alone
provider credential setup
privacy readiness claims

decisions.decision: The initial app-surface posture is not child-directed and does not target family-program distribution. Children, family, age-gated, or child-directed claims require separate owner approval, external review, regional policy mapping, ads restrictions, analytics restrictions, store metadata mapping, validator coverage, and proof evidence.
permits: future children and family policy analysis
forbids: child-directed product claims
family program readiness claims
child-directed ads or analytics readiness claims

decisions.decision: Consent management remains provider-neutral by default. No CMP or UMP provider is selected for implementation. Any CMP or UMP integration requires privacy data inventory, regional consent mapping, ads and analytics decisions where applicable, external review, validator coverage, and proof evidence.
permits: future CMP and UMP provider comparison
forbids: CMP setup from this decision alone
UMP setup from this decision alone
legal compliance readiness claims

decisions.decision: TanStack Query is the preferred query and cache library for future shared TypeScript and web client implementation after implementation authority exists. Mobile use remains subject to Expo compatibility and the mobile adapter gate. Query behaviour must remain an adapter over USF command, query, cache, retry, idempotency, tenant, permission, and privacy semantics.
forbids: dependency installation from this decision alone
cache semantics that override USF authority
query readiness claims without validators
downstreamEvaluationAndExecutionRequirem: mobile and web adapter gates close where applicable

decisions.decision: The default UI-only state model is local component state, route state, and explicit view-model state. A global UI-only store library is not selected by default and may be introduced only for non-authoritative UI state when a concrete implementation requirement justifies it.
permits: future global UI-only store exception analysis
forbids: global UI store dependency installation from this decision alone
using UI-only state as product authority
readiness claims based on UI state shape

decisions.decision: USF is not globally offline-first by default. App surfaces may support offline-tolerant read caches and explicit offline-safe UI states. Offline mutation queues are allowed only for capability-specific idempotent command envelopes with retention, purge, conflict, replay, tenant, permission, audit, and proof semantics.
forbids: general offline-first readiness claims
offline mutation queues without idempotency semantics
sync engine implementation from this decision alone

ownerDecisionIssueMayCloseWhen: the issue maps to one decision in this artefact
the Linear issue records checked acceptance criteria
the issue comment records that the decision is semantic only
downstream implementation and readiness gates remain separately requires evidence
implementationGateMayCloseWhen: all prerequisite semantic artefacts parse as strict JSON where applicable
all prerequisite owner decisions are closed or explicitly recorded as nonblocking with USF authority
validators and proof expectations required by the gate are identified
no implementation/runtime code is created by the gate closure itself
